title: 2026-11-05_Rhombus_Botnet_Investigation_a69
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity originating from several Linux hosts in your organization's infrastructure. Initial analysis suggests these hosts may be compromised by the Rhombus botnet, a Linux DDoS botnet targeting VPS and IoT devices. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activities, and implement appropriate containment measures.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Linux command line and system administration.
Understanding of network security principles and common attack vectors.
outcomes: Enumerate and analyze running services and systemd timers to identify suspicious activities.
Investigate network connections and service configurations to determine communication endpoints.
Identify and disable persistence mechanisms to prevent unauthorized activities from restarting.
Contain the threat by blocking unauthorized network communication.
Terminate malicious processes and remove malicious artifacts to remediate the compromise.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity originating from several Linux hosts in your organization's infrastructure. Initial analysis suggests these hosts may be compromised by the Rhombus botnet, a Linux DDoS botnet targeting VPS and IoT devices. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activities, and implement appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: SSH access is available to the entry host `bot1`. Use the username `investigator` and password `Rhombus2023!` to log in and begin your investigation. Enter 'start' to proceed.
levels.local_content: SSH access is available to the entry host `bot1`. Use the username `investigator` and password `Rhombus2023!` to log in and begin your investigation. Enter 'start' to proceed.

levels.title: Identify the C2 Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the entry host `bot1` using the provided credentials.
2. Enumerate all running and inactive services using the following command:
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
3. Look for unfamiliar service names or misspellings of legitimate services. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or startup behavior.
4. Identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server. The hidden flag is the name of this service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the status of suspicious services using `systemctl status <service>`.

levels.title: Determine the Communication Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. From the entry host `bot1`, inspect the service identified in the previous task using the following command:
   ```
systemctl cat <service>
```
2. Pay particular attention to the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
3. Check the script to find the communication port with the C2 server. The hidden flag is the port number.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat <service>` to view the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Inspect the script specified in `ExecStart` to find the communication port.

levels.title: Identify the Persistence Timer
levels.content: Investigators suspect that the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. From the entry host `bot1`, list all systemd timers using the following command:
   ```
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Identify the timer associated with the C2 beacon service. The hidden flag is the name of this timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with names related to the C2 beacon service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the status of suspicious timers using `systemctl status <timer>`.
